resources.string: Pause when you look away, and find where you left off. Optional, processed on your phone.
Eye detection on · tap to turn off
Eye detection off · tap to turn on

Uses the front camera during visible playback. Estimates can be wrong: this does not identify you or diagnose sleep. Images are never saved or sent by this feature. Android shows the camera indicator.
Allow camera access to enable this feature. You can change this in Android settings.
Resume automatically when I open my eyes
Brief blinks and winks do not pause playback. By default, tap to resume after prolonged closure.
Keeps one recovery point per video for up to 30 days, with a maximum of 100. Incognito points stay in memory only. Does not change your watched status.
Pause after eyes stay closed for
Look for my return while paused for
After this time the camera closes and a tap is required to resume.
Look at the screen as you normally would, in any comfortable position. Adaptation is optional and lasts only for this viewing. When a reading is uncertain, playback is left alone.
Adapt to how I am watching
Back to where I was watching
Start a regular video to try this feature. Unavailable in PiP, Cast, rooms, live streams and Shorts.
Experimental · verify it in your usual viewing conditions
Attention suspended to protect video smoothness
Pause and help me find my place when I look away.
Keep playing without alerts and save estimated attention intervals.

Five-second intervals with gaze present, absent, eyes closed or uncertain. Saved locally and included in settings backups; never saved in incognito. These estimates do not change watched status or playback progress.
Unable to update local attention data. Check available storage and try again.
Your viewing progress, watched status and recovery points stay available.
Detection only on · tap to turn off
Estimate attention while playback continues, without interruptions. Local and optional.
